_doc: Selection source of truth. Edit here, then run render-flags.py. Order is significant (last-one-wins on the final command line). Per-family override: add "gcc": false or "clang": false to an entry.

entries.comment: meta-warning about analysis limits, not code
GCC 14 analyzer self-debug output, not diagnostics
verbosity knob, noise in teaching output

header: Clang CFI requires -flto and a visibility setting IN THE SAME invocation —
probed alone, -fsanitize=cfi always fails ("only allowed with -flto") and
every entry here was silently filtered out. Each line below is one probe
unit (generate-flags.sh probes a whole line together and emits it together).
Note: on Linux this also needs an LTO-capable linker (lld or the LLVM gold
plugin); macOS ld64 and FreeBSD lld handle LTO natively. Where the linker
can't do LTO, these probes fail and CFI is skipped for that machine —
which is exactly the cache doing its job.

PIE/ASLR hardening for executables (companion to -fPIC for libraries); verified to compile+link cleanly alongside -fPIC
masks uninitialized reads from MSan/analyzer — we WANT those caught
hardening, not correctness detection; register-wipe cost
umbrella flag; would fight our explicit FORTIFY/PIE choices
traps instead of diagnostics; we want messages
clang 20: stricter aliasing OPTIMIZATION — widens UB exploitation, against our -fno-fast-math philosophy
numerics behavior knob, default is correct
GCC >= 13: __builtin_unreachable becomes a trap, not UB
TBAA OPTIMIZATION — widens UB exploitation, same call as -fpointer-tbaa
GCC: honor signaling NaN semantics (pairs with -ftrapping-math)

header: DataFlowSanitizer (clang-only, x86-64 Linux). The -dfsan-* switches are
LLVM-internal options: as bare driver flags they are "unused arguments"
and every one was silently filtered out. They must be passed via -mllvm,
together with the sanitizer itself — each line is one probe unit.
Exactly ONE debug-level flag: they override each other (last one wins),
and the old set even included -ggdb0, which turns debug info OFF.

entries.flags: -ggdb3 = richest info (includes macro definitions) targeted at gdb.

clang >= 20: variables stay inspectable in debugger
inverse of above — REDUCES debug info
Windows PDB format, not our platforms
GCC: track uninitialized vars in debug info
GCC: emit per-function stack usage (.su files in build dir)
keep every function inspectable in the debugger
clang: macro definitions in debug info
clang: complete type info, no vendor elision
GCC: callgraph with stack usage + dynamic allocation

makes clang treat EVERY comment (incl. plain /* license/email headers) as a doc comment, so -Wdocumentation-unknown-command fires on the @ in emails across 200+ files. Marginal value, high false-positive cost -> excluded.
clang: embed source in DWARF5 — debugger always has it
ARM MTE hardware only — no current platform has it

header: Compiler-accepted hardening flags (always on; no link-only switches here)

entries.comment: stronger stack-probing than -fstack-check on Linux x86/ARM; per-compiler probe drops it where unsupported (e.g. macOS)
GCC on some targets; clang usually no
GCC >= 14: scrub stack frames on exit
tuning knob; base -fharden-control-flow-redundancy default is sane
Spectre-v1 (bounds-check bypass) mitigation, clang. Runtime-perf cost; deployment hardening, not a correctness/diagnostic win — off for the teaching build, flip on per policy.
Spectre-v2 (branch-target injection) mitigation, clang/x86. Perf cost; off by default (deployment hardening).
Spectre-v2 mitigation, gcc/x86 (retpoline thunks). Perf cost; off by default.
Retbleed mitigation, gcc/x86. Perf cost; off by default.
Straight-line-speculation hardening, gcc+clang (x86/arm). Off by default (deployment hardening).
Enables the CET shadow-stack ISA, x86; complements -fcf-protection=full (already on). Off by default; enable per deployment policy.

header: Linker hardening + diagnostics. Probe mode is LINK, so each platform keeps
what its linker accepts: ELF linkers (Linux/FreeBSD) take the -z family,
macOS ld64 rejects it and simply drops off that machine's cache.

entries.comment: resolve all symbols at load (full RELRO with relro)
code pages never share with data
export symbols so backtraces have names
forbid undefined symbols — BREAKS sanitizer runtimes (resolved at load)

header: NSan (clang >= 20): detects floating-point precision loss numerically.
RTSan (clang >= 20): flags blocking calls inside [[clang::nonblocking]]
functions. A no-op until code is annotated, but costs nothing to enable.
TySan (clang >= 20): detects type-based aliasing violations at runtime.

entries.comment: trap-mode dedup knob; we don't use trap mode

header: https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-13.2.0/gcc/Warning-Options.html

entries.comment: ...then =2 so GCC ends on the stronger level

gcc-only: -Wstrict-flex-arrays is ignored unless -fstrict-flex-arrays is present, so the two are probed+emitted as one group (=3 = only [] is a flexible array member). clang lacks the warning, so the whole group is dropped on clang.
Style: force all declarations to the top of a block, before any statements (variables-before-code). Deliberate house style, not an old-C requirement — works the same in C17/18.
LAST on purpose: value forms above are GCC-only; last-wins must end widest (plain = =global)
contradicts the deliberate -Wno- form above (driver-noise suppression)
ORDER: plain form after =2 would downgrade GCC to level 1; clang gets it below
CONFLICT: 0 DISABLES; -Wstrict-aliasing=3 is the live setting

clang C++ safe-buffers hardening (pointer-arithmetic-on-buffer). Kept for C++ (real fix: std::span/std::array); denied for C via overrides-c.txt because in C it fires on every ptr[i] with no hardened-container alternative. gcc lacks it, so g++ drops it at probe time.
companion to -Wunsafe-buffer-usage; same C++-only scoping via c:false.
contradicts the deliberate -Wno- form (e.g. clang warns  -pg unused  at compile)

gcc-16 style warning: flags runs of >=8 consecutive leading spaces, i.e. it wants tab-based indentation. This codebase indents with 4 spaces (clang-format-enforced), so it fires on every 2nd-level line. Off — conflicts with the house style; -Wtrailing-whitespace=blanks stays (it agrees with the style and never fires here).

GCC 16 warning for functions that intentionally wrap allocators. The p101 C library deliberately provides malloc/calloc/realloc wrappers for error handling and resource tracking, so this warning conflicts with the library design. GCC also emits it but rejects it in #pragma GCC diagnostic, so keep it out of generated warning flags.
policy warning: fires on ANY template use
policy warning: fires on ANY namespace use
policy warning: fires on ANY MI use
policy warning: fires on ANY VI use
deprecated ALIAS of -Wshadow=local — would override the ordered =global block above
